name: Gestao Hospital
description: We need an API to organize a public health system, specifically to assist the Unified Health System (SUS) in Brazil. The goal is to create a tool that helps avoid waste and optimize resources based on patient needs. The system should manage hospital information, including their stock of products, blood banks, and available beds. It should be able to recommend the closest hospital with available beds to a patient and facilitate the transfer of products, such as blood, between nearby hospitals if one is in need. A hospital with four or fewer items or liters of a product is considered to have only enough for its own use. The API should allow for registering hospitals, indicating the closest hospital to a patient's location, managing patient check-in and check-out, checking available beds, and managing product and blood bank inventories within hospitals.
highLevelGoals: The Hospital Administrator needs to efficiently manage the hospital's stock of products, blood banks, and available beds to ensure optimal resource utilization and avoid waste.
The Hospital Administrator aims to streamline patient check-in and check-out processes and effectively manage available beds to improve patient care and operational efficiency.

The Hospital Administrator needs to facilitate the transfer of products, such as blood, between nearby hospitals when their hospital is in need or can provide assistance, ensuring critical resources are available where required.
The Medical Professional needs to quickly identify the closest hospital with available beds for a patient to ensure timely and appropriate care.
The Medical Professional aims to effectively coordinate patient transfers to appropriate facilities based on resource availability and patient needs.
The Medical Professional needs to ensure the availability of critical medical supplies, including blood, by being able to identify hospitals that can provide or receive such products.
The SUS Coordinator needs to optimize the allocation of resources across the entire public health system to avoid waste and ensure equitable distribution based on patient needs.
The SUS Coordinator aims to monitor and manage the transfer of products and patients between hospitals at a macro level to ensure efficient operation of the Unified Health System.

The SUS Coordinator needs to gain comprehensive insights into system-wide statistics, including hospital stock levels, blood bank inventories, and bed availability, to make informed strategic decisions.
lowLevelGoals: The Hospital Administrator updates the quantity of a specific product in the hospital's inventory.
The Hospital Administrator views the current stock levels of all products in the hospital.
